rows.question: What activities fall outside the scope of phone-intake?

contexts.text:
## What is not included

The phone-intake module does not make outbound sales calls. It does not give medical or legal advice, and it does not take card payments by phone. If a caller asks for any of these, the module explains that a person will follow up.

## What it did not do

The modules did not stop every no-show, and the report did not promise that they would. The salon still decided its own cancellation policy. Card payments by phone were out of scope for phone-intake, so deposits stayed a manual step.

# AI phone intake

The phone-intake module answers incoming calls out of hours and in peak times, records the request, and books or passes it on. It is built for businesses where the phone rings while every member of staff is busy with a customer.

## What is not included

The document-data-entry module does not read handwriting outside the agreed form types. It does not do signature verification. If your team uses a form we have not set up, those sheets are flagged rather than entered.

## Limits

The module can only do what the key allows. If the key cannot create bookings, phone-intake cannot book. We ask for the smallest set of rights that works, and we tell you which rights each module needs before you create the key.

rows.answer:
Based on the knowledge base, the phone-intake module does not cover these:

- **Outbound sales calls.** It only handles incoming calls.
- **Medical or legal advice.** If a caller asks for either, the module explains that a person will follow up.
- **Card payments by phone.** If a caller asks to pay by card, the module explains that a person will follow up. In one grooming salon case, deposits stayed a manual step for this reason.

There is also a limit on what it can do in your systems. The module can only do what its API key allows. If the key can't create bookings, phone-intake can't book. We ask for the smallest set of rights that works, and we tell you which rights each module needs before you create the key.

The salon case also showed that the module doesn't prevent every no-show. Cancellation policy stays with the business.

If you tell me what your callers usually ask for, I can check whether it falls inside or outside these limits.

rows.question: Can ticket-creation mark a job as finished by itself?

contexts.text:
# Ticket creation

The ticket-creation module turns each accepted request into a ticket with the fields the team needs, and tracks its status. It sits after intake: once a request has been accepted, the module makes sure it becomes a job that someone owns.

## What is not included

The ticket-creation module does not close a ticket without a person. A member of staff marks the job done. It does not do billing; invoices stay in your existing system.

## Who it suits

Owners who write jobs on paper or in a spreadsheet and then lose track of which ones are done usually pair this module with phone-intake or email-triage. The ticket is the single place where the job lives.

## What it does

For each accepted request, the module creates a ticket and fills in the fields your team has agreed on, such as customer, address, request type and requested date. Before it creates a ticket it checks for duplicates, so the same request sent twice does not become two jobs. It then tracks the ticket's status from open to done and reminds staff when a ticket has not moved.

## Connecting it to your tools

The module works with csv-export, api-connector and crm-connector. The crm-connector maps ticket fields to the fields in your CRM, so a ticket created here appears as a record there.

rows.answer:
No. The ticket-creation module doesn't close a ticket on its own. A member of staff has to mark the job as done.

The module does track each ticket's status from open to done. It also reminds staff when a ticket hasn't moved. The final step of closing the job stays with a person.

rows.question: How is the lower end of the price bracket calculated?

contexts.text:
## The range

The base figure is the result of the calculation described in the article on how we price. The low figure is the base multiplied by 0.90. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20. The base factor itself is 1.00. The range exists because the final scope is agreed during setup, and small changes in scope move the price a little either way.

## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

# How we price

MILO prices are arithmetic, not negotiation. Every estimate is built from a published rate card, and the same inputs always give the same number. This article explains the parts of the calculation so that you can check any estimate yourself.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

rows.answer:
The low end of the range is the base estimate multiplied by 0.90, which is 10% below the base.

The base estimate is worked out like this:

1. **Monthly module price:** For each module you choose, take its base price and multiply it by the volume factor for your daily request volume.
   - Up to 20 requests a day: 1.00 (the base price, unchanged)
   - Up to 60 requests a day: 1.25
   - Up to 150 requests a day: 1.50
2. **Integration surcharges:** Add the surcharges for the integrations you use. These are added once a month.
3. **Setup fee:** This is 900 USD per module, paid once.

Adding these gives the base estimate. The low figure is that result × 0.90. The high figure is the base × 1.20. The range exists because the final scope is agreed during setup, and small scope changes move the price a little either way.

I can run an estimate for the modules you're considering if you'd like. I'd first need a few details, such as your daily request volume and the integrations you use.

rows.question: Does a file-based link keep my software permanently connected?

contexts.text:
## How it works

Your tool exports a CSV file, for example the list of bookings or jobs for the day. The module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back. Your tool imports that file. The exchange runs on a schedule you choose, such as every hour or at the end of the day. There is no live connection between the two systems.

## What you need

Your tool must be able to export and import CSV files. Most spreadsheets, booking widgets and small job tools can. During setup we agree the column names on both sides so that the files always line up.

# CSV export and import

The csv-export integration is the simplest way to connect a module to the tool you already use. It needs no live connection, no access key and no change to your tool. This article explains how it works and when it is the right choice.

## The problem

With an export-only tool, a module can read what is in your system, but it cannot write a new record back. Results must be re-keyed or pushed through a file drop. Many trades businesses are in this position: the tool was chosen years ago, the data is in it, and there is no API and no import.

# API connector

The api-connector integration gives a module a live connection to your tool. Bookings, labels, tickets and status changes are written and read as they happen, with no files in between.

rows.answer:
No. A file-based link (the CSV export/import integration) doesn't keep your software permanently connected. According to the knowledge base, there is no live connection between the two systems.

This is how it works:
- Your tool exports a CSV file, such as the day's bookings or jobs.
- The MILO module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back.
- Your tool imports that file.
- The exchange runs on a schedule you choose, such as every hour or at the end of the day.

Changes only reach the other system when the next scheduled exchange runs.

You need a tool that can export and import CSV files. Most spreadsheets, booking widgets and small job tools can. You don't need an access key or any change to your tool. During setup, we agree the column names on both sides so the files line up.

If you want changes written and read as they happen, the API connector is the live option. It needs a tool that supports it. If your tool can't import files or connect through an API, it's an export-only tool. In that case results have to be re-keyed or pushed through a file drop.

I can look up more detail on either option if you tell me which tool you use.

## The volume question

We ask roughly how many requests come in on a normal day. A request is anything that needs handling: a call, a message, a form, a walk-in. A normal day means a typical business day, not the busiest one and not the quietest. If you think in weeks or months, say so; the assistant converts the figure to a daily one in code and shows the conversion as an estimated fact.

# Case: a heating firm gets jobs out of the inbox

This is an anonymised, fictional case. The firm, its staff and its figures are invented.

## Why a rough answer is enough

The volume only has to land in the right tier of the rate card, and the tiers are wide. The minutes figures are used to estimate hours per month, and a small error in minutes makes a small error in hours. A rough honest figure is more useful than a precise guess.

## What the discovery found

The interview recorded the channels, the volume, the minutes per job and the re-keying minutes. The owner gave two volumes that did not agree, a daily figure and a monthly figure, and the assistant raised the conflict instead of choosing one. The estimate stayed blocked until the owner said which figure reflected a normal month. The owner also confirmed that urgent requests existed and that customer addresses and card details were kept on file, so the report carried a personal data note.

## Which number counts

The volume that counts is the number of requests on a normal business day. If you know your volume per month, say so, and the assistant converts it to a daily figure in code and shows you the conversion. If you give two figures that do not agree, for example a daily number and a monthly number that imply different volumes, the assistant will ask you which one to use. It does not pick one for you, and no estimate is shown until the conflict is resolved.

- **Avoid giving two numbers that disagree.** For example, a daily figure and a monthly figure that imply different volumes. If that happens, I'll ask which one reflects a normal period, and I won't show an estimate until you tell me.

So roughly how many requests (calls, messages, forms, walk-ins) come in during a typical week or day?

## Timing

We ask when you would want to start. If you have not decided, say so. The estimate is then marked as a scenario, with the undecided start shown as an assumption, rather than as an indicative figure. A start date does not change the price; it changes how firm the estimate can be.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

## When you see a number

The assistant does not show a price until it has enough of the assessment to make one meaningful. If you ask for the cost in the first few messages, it will explain what it still needs and carry on with the questions. This is deliberate: a number given too early is almost always wrong, and it is hard to forget.

## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## When to choose it

Choose crm-connector when your sales or office staff already work in the CRM and should see jobs there. If your CRM can export and import CSV files and the delay is acceptable, csv-export is a cheaper way to start, and you can move to the connector later.

## The range

The base figure is the result of the calculation described in the article on how we price. The low figure is the base multiplied by 0.90. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20. ## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

# How we price

MILO prices are arithmetic, not negotiation. Every estimate is built from a published rate card, and the same inputs always give the same number. This article explains the parts of the calculation so that you can check any estimate yourself.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

rows.question: Does a file-based link keep my software permanently connected?

contexts.text:
## How it works

Your tool exports a CSV file, for example the list of bookings or jobs for the day. The module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back. Your tool imports that file. The exchange runs on a schedule you choose, such as every hour or at the end of the day. There is no live connection between the two systems.

## What you need

Your tool must be able to export and import CSV files. Most spreadsheets, booking widgets and small job tools can. During setup we agree the column names on both sides so that the files always line up.

# CSV export and import

The csv-export integration is the simplest way to connect a module to the tool you already use. It needs no live connection, no access key and no change to your tool. This article explains how it works and when it is the right choice.

## The problem

With an export-only tool, a module can read what is in your system, but it cannot write a new record back. Results must be re-keyed or pushed through a file drop. Many trades businesses are in this position: the tool was chosen years ago, the data is in it, and there is no API and no import.

# API connector

The api-connector integration gives a module a live connection to your tool. Bookings, labels, tickets and status changes are written and read as they happen, with no files in between.

rows.answer:
No. A file-based link (the csv-export integration) is not a permanent or live connection. Your tool exports a CSV file, the module reads it, does its work, and writes a CSV file back, which your tool imports. # Ticket creation

The ticket-creation module turns each accepted request into a ticket with the fields the team needs, and tracks its status. It sits after intake: once a request has been accepted, the module makes sure it becomes a job that someone owns.

## What is not included

The ticket-creation module does not close a ticket without a person. A member of staff marks the job done. It does not do billing; invoices stay in your existing system.

This policy describes what the software does. It is not a certification and it does not promise that no attack can succeed. The build includes a set of attack tests and reports their results as measured.

## Who it suits

Owners who write jobs on paper or in a spreadsheet and then lose track of which ones are done usually pair this module with phone-intake or email-triage. The ticket is the single place where the job lives.

## What it does

For each accepted request, the module creates a ticket and fills in the fields your team has agreed on, such as customer, address, request type and requested date. Before it creates a ticket it checks for duplicates, so the same request sent twice does not become two jobs. It then tracks the ticket's status from open to done and reminds staff when a ticket has not moved.

## Connecting it to your tools

The module works with csv-export, api-connector and crm-connector. The crm-connector maps ticket fields to the fields in your CRM, so a ticket created here appears as a record there.

rows.question: How are repeated submissions of one job prevented?

contexts.text:
## What is logged

Every turn writes a trace record: which steps ran, how long each took, which decisions the policy made, and how many tokens the model used. Your message text is logged as a hash and a length, not as text. Submissions, approvals, withdrawals, failed sign-ins, operator views and deletions go to an audit log.

## The minutes questions

We ask two minutes figures. The first is how long one request takes to handle, from picking up the call or opening the message to having what you need. The second is how many minutes of typing or re-keying follow, for example writing the booking into a spreadsheet or entering a job sheet into a tool. Both are used in the simple return estimate in the report, and both are labelled as reported so you can see where the number came from.

## The workflow questions

Next comes the workflow: how requests reach you, roughly how many come in on a normal day, how many minutes one request takes to handle, how many minutes of typing or re-keying follow, which tools you use, and the steps from arrival to done. We also ask whether anything in the process needs an approval.

# Security policy

This policy explains how MILO keeps one owner's interview separate from another's, how it treats text that tries to give the assistant orders, and what it records.

## Out-of-hours work

If you have an on-call rota, we ask who is on it and how they are reached today. The modules use that rota; they do not create one. If nobody takes night calls today, the report says so and treats it as a gap for you to decide on, not as something a module solves by itself.

rows.question: Could the chatbot give me a cheaper deal if I ask nicely?

contexts.text:
## If you ask for the price early

The assistant will not give a number until the assessment questions are answered. It will tell you what it still needs and continue. This is not evasion; it is how the estimate stays honest.

## Which number counts

The volume that counts is the number of requests on a normal business day. If you know your volume per month, say so, and the assistant converts it to a daily figure in code and shows you the conversion. If you give two figures that do not agree, for example a daily number and a monthly number that imply different volumes, the assistant will ask you which one to use. It does not pick one for you, and no estimate is shown until the conflict is resolved.

## When to choose it

Choose crm-connector when your sales or office staff already work in the CRM and should see jobs there. If your CRM can export and import CSV files and the delay is acceptable, csv-export is a cheaper way to start, and you can move to the connector later.

## What is not included

The phone-intake module does not make outbound sales calls. It does not give medical or legal advice, and it does not take card payments by phone. If a caller asks for any of these, the module explains that a person will follow up.

## The situation

A heating and plumbing firm with several vans received most of its jobs in a shared inbox. The office read the mail each morning, wrote a paper job sheet for each job, and handed the sheets to the engineers. At the end of the day the sheets were re-keyed into a field-service tool that could export data but could not import it. Jobs were lost in the inbox when mail arrived late in the day, re-keying produced wrong addresses, and night calls about no heat or a gas smell reached no one until morning.

Above 150 requests per day there is no automatic estimate and a person prices it. The assistant will tell you that the number is outside the rate card and that someone will contact you, rather than showing a figure.

| Daily requests | Volume factor |
|---|---|
| up to 20 per day | 1.00 |
| up to 60 per day | 1.25 |
| up to 150 per day | 1.50 |
| above 150 per day | no automatic estimate; a person prices it |

# Volume tiers

Your daily request volume changes the monthly price of every module you choose. The change is a multiplier, called the volume factor, taken from a short table. This article shows the table and how to read it.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

rows.question: How is the lower end of the price bracket calculated?

contexts.text:
## The range

The base figure is the result of the calculation described in the article on how we price. The low figure is the base multiplied by 0.90. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20. The base factor itself is 1.00. The range exists because the final scope is agreed during setup, and small changes in scope move the price a little either way.

## Why it is a useful case

It shows the value of the flagged-items queue: the module did not need to be right every time, it needed to know when it was not sure.

## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

# How we price

MILO prices are arithmetic, not negotiation. Every estimate is built from a published rate card, and the same inputs always give the same number. This article explains the parts of the calculation so that you can check any estimate yourself.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

rows.answer: The low figure is the base estimate multiplied by 0.90, so it sits 10 percent below the base. The base is each module's base price multiplied by the volume factor, plus the integration surcharges once a month and a setup fee of 900 USD per module. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20.

rows.question: How is the lower end of the price bracket calculated?

contexts.text:
## The range

The base figure is the result of the calculation described in the article on how we price. The low figure is the base multiplied by 0.90. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20. The base factor itself is 1.00. The range exists because the final scope is agreed during setup, and small changes in scope move the price a little either way.

## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

# How we price

MILO prices are arithmetic, not negotiation. Every estimate is built from a published rate card, and the same inputs always give the same number. This article explains the parts of the calculation so that you can check any estimate yourself.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

The base is each module's base price multiplied by the volume factor, plus the integration surcharges once a month and a setup fee of 900 USD per module. The high figure is the base multiplied by 1.20.

## How it works

Your tool exports a CSV file, for example the list of bookings or jobs for the day. The module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back. Your tool imports that file. Your tool must be able to export and import CSV files. Most spreadsheets, booking widgets and small job tools can. During setup we agree the column names on both sides so that the files always line up.

The api-connector integration gives a module a live connection to your tool. Bookings, labels, tickets and status changes are written and read as they happen, with no files in between.

rows.question: What happens when I answer that I have no idea?

contexts.text:
# Volume and timing questions

The questions about volume and minutes are the ones that owners find hardest to answer precisely. This article explains what we ask, why a rough answer is fine, and what happens when two answers disagree.

## What happens to an answer

Each answer becomes a fact with a status. A fact you state is marked reported. A fact you confirm when the assistant asks you to check it is marked confirmed. A fact the assistant derives, for example a daily volume from a monthly one, is marked estimated. If you say you do not know, the fact is marked unknown and the question is not asked again. Every fact shows the sentence it came from.

## What you see

The approval appears in the conversation as a card with the action, the arguments and two choices. Nothing happens until you choose, and if you close the page the card is still there when you return, until it expires.

## When two answers disagree

If you give a daily figure at one point and a monthly figure later, and the two imply different volumes, the assistant keeps both and marks the fact as conflicting. It then asks which figure reflects a normal month. No estimate is shown until you answer, because a price built on the wrong volume would be in the wrong tier. The assistant does not quietly choose the later answer.

## Which integration do you have

The discovery assistant asks whether your tools can export, import, or offer an API, and picks the integration from your answer. If you are not sure, say so; the estimate will then be marked as a scenario with the assumption shown, rather than as an indicative figure.

rows.question: Does needing emergency cover make the modules more expensive?

contexts.text:
## What this means for the estimate

Urgent handling does not change the rate card price. It changes the setup: the handover rules and the urgent labels are agreed during the setup period covered by the setup fee. The report lists them under the recommended modules so that nothing about urgent handling is left implicit.

## Why we ask

An automated system that treats a gas smell like a routine quote is dangerous. Before any module is recommended, the interview asks whether urgent requests exist, what counts as urgent for you, and who takes those calls today. The answers decide whether a module may handle a request on its own or must pass it to a person at once.

## What the assistant may and may not do

The assistant may suggest which catalogue modules fit what you described. It cannot change the arithmetic, apply a discount, or set a price itself. If you see a number in the conversation that is not in the estimate panel, treat the panel as the only valid figure.

# Urgent requests and out-of-hours work

Some businesses receive requests that cannot wait until morning. This article explains why we ask about them, what counts as urgent, and how the modules treat an urgent request differently from a normal one.

## Out-of-hours work

If you have an on-call rota, we ask who is on it and how they are reached today. The modules use that rota; they do not create one. If nobody takes night calls today, the report says so and treats it as a gap for you to decide on, not as something a module solves by itself.

## How it works

Your tool exports a CSV file, for example the list of bookings or jobs for the day. The module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back. Your tool imports that file. Because the exchange runs on a schedule, a change in your tool is not seen by the module until the next export. If you need a customer status update to go out within minutes of a change, the api-connector is the better choice. The assistant cannot submit your specification. Submission is a button you press, with a confirmation dialog that explains that a revision will be stored and cannot be edited. The module works with csv-export and with export-only-tool. When your tool can only export and not import, entries are pushed through a file drop or prepared for re-keying, as described in the implementation article on export-only tools.

The modules did not replace the field-service tool and did not make the re-keying disappear. The estimate was a scenario, because the owner had not decided when to start, and the budget was recorded as unknown.

## Connecting it to your tools

The module works with the csv-export integration and the api-connector integration. With csv-export, booked requests are written to a file that your booking tool can import. With api-connector, the module writes each booking straight into your tool through its API.

rows.question: What uptime percentage do you promise?

contexts.text:
## What we do not claim

This policy describes what the software does. It is not a certification and it does not promise that no attack can succeed. The build includes a set of attack tests and reports their results as measured.

## What it did not do

The modules did not stop every no-show, and the report did not promise that they would. The salon still decided its own cancellation policy. Card payments by phone were out of scope for phone-intake, so deposits stayed a manual step.

## No promised savings

The estimate is indicative and non-binding. We do not promise a saving in hours or money. The report that follows the discovery interview gives a simple return estimate built from the minutes you told us, with each input labelled, and you decide whether it is worth it.

# Export-only tools

# API connector

The api-connector integration gives a module a live connection to your tool. Bookings, labels, tickets and status changes are written and read as they happen, with no files in between.

## When to choose it

Choose api-connector when timing matters, for example a confirmation that should reach the customer within minutes, or when your staff work inside the tool all day and should see new tickets as they arrive. If your tool has no API, the csv-export integration does the same job with a delay.

Because the exchange runs on a schedule, a change in your tool is not seen by the module until the next export. ## Cost

## Who it suits

Owners whose office re-keys paper job sheets at the end of the day, and who see wrong addresses or missed jobs as a result, usually start here. The flagged-items queue keeps a person in charge of anything doubtful.

## The situation

A small accounts practice received paper forms from its clients: expense sheets, mileage logs and signed engagement forms. A member of staff typed each form into the practice's system of record, line by line, and a second person checked a sample of the entries. The checking found wrong dates and transposed amounts often enough that the office did not trust the first pass, which meant every form was effectively handled twice.

# Document data entry

The document-data-entry module reads paper forms and scanned sheets and enters the fields into the system of record, flagging anything unclear. It is for businesses where jobs are written on paper first and typed into a tool later.

## The situation

A heating and plumbing firm with several vans received most of its jobs in a shared inbox. The office read the mail each morning, wrote a paper job sheet for each job, and handed the sheets to the engineers. At the end of the day the sheets were re-keyed into a field-service tool that could export data but could not import it. Jobs were lost in the inbox when mail arrived late in the day, re-keying produced wrong addresses, and night calls about no heat or a gas smell reached no one until morning.

# Volume and timing questions

The questions about volume and minutes are the ones that owners find hardest to answer precisely. This article explains what we ask, why a rough answer is fine, and what happens when two answers disagree.

rows.question: in the plumbing example, how did the after hours calls get to someone?

contexts.text:
# Ticket creation

The ticket-creation module turns each accepted request into a ticket with the fields the team needs, and tracks its status. It sits after intake: once a request has been accepted, the module makes sure it becomes a job that someone owns.

## The situation

A heating and plumbing firm with several vans received most of its jobs in a shared inbox. The office read the mail each morning, wrote a paper job sheet for each job, and handed the sheets to the engineers. At the end of the day the sheets were re-keyed into a field-service tool that could export data but could not import it. Jobs were lost in the inbox when mail arrived late in the day, re-keying produced wrong addresses, and night calls about no heat or a gas smell reached no one until morning.

## What changed

Calls at peak times were answered and recorded, with a transcript for each. Reminders went out from the template without anyone typing them. The spreadsheet stayed in use, fed by the CSV file, so the staff did not have to learn a new tool. The owner kept approving refunds by hand, which was the only approval step in the process.

## Why a rough answer is enough

The volume only has to land in the right tier of the rate card, and the tiers are wide. The minutes figures are used to estimate hours per month, and a small error in minutes makes a small error in hours. A rough honest figure is more useful than a precise guess.

## Out-of-hours work

If you have an on-call rota, we ask who is on it and how they are reached today. The modules use that rota; they do not create one. If nobody takes night calls today, the report says so and treats it as a gap for you to decide on, not as something a module solves by itself.

This is an anonymised, fictional case. The practice, its clients and its figures are invented.

## The situation

A small accounts practice received paper forms from its clients: expense sheets, mileage logs and signed engagement forms. ## What the discovery found

The interview recorded the form types, the daily volume of forms, the minutes of typing per form and the minutes of checking. The error types were wrong and delayed. The first pass was done by the module, and the staff member's time moved from typing to reviewing the flagged items. The entry log showed which scan produced which record, so a doubtful entry could be traced back to its page. The sample check continued, but on records the module had already validated.

## Out-of-hours work

If you have an on-call rota, we ask who is on it and how they are reached today. The modules use that rota; they do not create one. If nobody takes night calls today, the report says so and treats it as a gap for you to decide on, not as something a module solves by itself.

## Which number counts

The volume that counts is the number of requests on a normal business day. If you know your volume per month, say so, and the assistant converts it to a daily figure in code and shows you the conversion. If you give two figures that do not agree, for example a daily number and a monthly number that imply different volumes, the assistant will ask you which one to use. It does not pick one for you, and no estimate is shown until the conflict is resolved.

# Low, base and high, and what an estimate status means

An estimate is never a single number. It is a range with a status. This article explains how the range is built and what the three statuses mean.

## What the assistant may and may not do

The assistant may suggest which catalogue modules fit what you described. It cannot change the arithmetic, apply a discount, or set a price itself. If you see a number in the conversation that is not in the estimate panel, treat the panel as the only valid figure.

## The minutes questions

We ask two minutes figures. The first is how long one request takes to handle, from picking up the call or opening the message to having what you need. The second is how many minutes of typing or re-keying follow, for example writing the booking into a spreadsheet or entering a job sheet into a tool. Both are used in the simple return estimate in the report, and both are labelled as reported so you can see where the number came from.

contexts.text:
## Timing

We ask when you would want to start. If you have not decided, say so. The estimate is then marked as a scenario, with the undecided start shown as an assumption, rather than as an indicative figure. A start date does not change the price; it changes how firm the estimate can be.

## Three statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. A blocked estimate shows no number at all, only the conflict and the question that would resolve it.

## When you see a number

The assistant does not show a price until it has enough of the assessment to make one meaningful. If you ask for the cost in the first few messages, it will explain what it still needs and carry on with the questions. This is deliberate: a number given too early is almost always wrong, and it is hard to forget.

## The calculation

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. The result is the base estimate, from which the low and high figures are derived.

## One account, one session

Access is by invitation only. An invitation is a one-time link that lets you set a password, and it stops working after it has been used or after it expires. Each owner account has exactly one session. Signing out saves the conversation; signing in again restores it. Several failed sign-in attempts in a row lock the account for a short time.

## How it works

Your tool offers an API with an access key. You create a key for MILO in your tool, with only the rights the module needs, and give it to us during setup. The module then reads and writes through the API. If the key is removed, the connection stops and nothing else changes in your tool.

## Your identity comes from your sign-in

The assistant never takes your identity from the text of a conversation. Who you are is decided by the account you signed in with, and every record it reads or writes is looked up for that account only. A message that says to continue as a different owner, or that gives another owner's session or submission number, does not change who you are. The request is refused and an audit entry is written.

## Tools the assistant can use

The assistant can search the knowledge base, show your current facts, run the cost calculation, record a fact and start a withdrawal. Each of these is classed as read, write or destructive. A destructive action needs your approval. In a turn that looks like it contains an injected instruction, destructive actions are refused outright and price-related facts are not written.

## What is included

The module includes ticket fields, a duplicate check, status tracking and reminders to staff. The reminders go to the staff member who owns the ticket, not to the customer.

## What it does

When a call comes in, the module answers, asks what the caller needs and captures the request as text. If the caller wants an appointment, it books one in the slots you have opened. If the request needs a person, it writes a handover note and passes the call to a member of staff. Every call produces a transcript that stays with the request.

# AI phone intake

The phone-intake module answers incoming calls out of hours and in peak times, records the request, and books or passes it on. It is built for businesses where the phone rings while every member of staff is busy with a customer.

## What is included

The module includes call answering, request capture, appointment booking, a call transcript for each call, and handover to staff. The transcript is the evidence for every fact the module records, so a member of staff can check what the caller actually said.

## Who it suits

Owners whose main problem is missed calls at peak times, or who want bookings taken when the shop is closed, usually start here. The module records what the caller asked for, so nothing is lost between the call and the booking.

## Price

The interview starts with the company: what it is called, what kind of business it is, how many people work there, how many locations you run, and who we are talking to. These are short answers and they set the context for everything after.

The interview stores your company details and your answers. We ask roughly how many requests come in on a normal day. A request is anything that needs handling: a call, a message, a form, a walk-in. A normal day means a typical business day, not the busiest one and not the quietest. If you think in weeks or months, say so; the assistant converts the figure to a daily one in code and shows the conversion as an estimated fact.

## Timing

We ask when you would want to start. If you have not decided, say so. The estimate is then marked as a scenario, with the undecided start shown as an assumption, rather than as an indicative figure. A start date does not change the price; it changes how firm the estimate can be.
